subject: Meteorology
title: Why Sunsets Are Red
description: A micro-lesson that makes Why Sunsets Are Red usable.

hook.text: At sunset, sunlight travels through up to 40 times more atmosphere than at noon—and the sky turns red.

buildup.text: The long path scatters away nearly all the blue light—only long-wavelength reds and oranges survive the journey.

discovery.text: The reddest sunsets occur when fine aerosols (dust, smoke, haze) enhance the scattering—removing even more blue.

twist.text: Volcanic eruptions inject aerosols into the stratosphere—producing vivid red and purple sunsets worldwide for months.

climax.text: After the 1883 Krakatoa eruption, sunsets were so red that fire departments were called to fight nonexistent fires.

punchline.text: The redder the sunset, the more atmosphere the light had to fight through.

quiz.question: Why do volcanic eruptions produce especially vivid sunsets?
options: Stratospheric aerosols enhance scattering of blue light
